description:
Lightweight, cloud-native GIS platform for visualizing and analyzing geospatial data

GeoLibre is a lightweight, cloud-native desktop GIS for visualizing and
analyzing geospatial data, built on MapLibre with deck.gl for 3D and
point-cloud overlays. It loads vector and raster files, web services, 3D
Tiles, MBTiles, and cloud-native formats, and is extensible through a plugin
ecosystem.
GeoLibre v3.9.0 lets the desktop AI Assistant run on your ChatGPT plan, keeps the assistant's conversation when you switch providers, and adds Gallery collections and a Summarize within tool. You can now sign in with ChatGPT instead of pasting an API key, browse curated collections of shared projects, count and summarize features inside polygons, and use GeoLibre in Traditional Chinese. It brings together 35 pull requests from 2 contributors. Thank you to everyone who helped!

## Highlights

• **Sign in with ChatGPT**：the desktop AI Assistant can use your ChatGPT plan instead of an API key. Sign-in runs in your system browser and the tokens stay in the system keychain; Settings shows the signed-in account, a link to usage, and sign-out. See [AI Assistant](https://geolibre.app/user-guide/ai-assistant/#signing-in-with-chatgpt-desktop).
• **An AI Assistant that keeps the thread**：switching profiles or models mid-conversation now carries the conversation over to the new provider instead of starting empty. A new `set_view` tool moves the camera to an exact center, zoom, rotation, and tilt, and the panel marks the default profile. See [AI Assistant](https://geolibre.app/user-guide/ai-assistant/).
• **Gallery collections**：Open from Gallery has a Collections tab that browses public collections from share.geolibre.app and opens their projects in place. See [Gallery](https://geolibre.app/gallery/).
• **Summarize within**：a new client-side Vector tool counts the features of another layer inside each polygon, summarizes a numeric field (sum, mean, min, max), and measures how much of each polygon other polygons cover, without double-counting overlaps. See [Processing](https://geolibre.app/user-guide/processing/).
• **Number columns that read like QGIS**：the attribute table right-aligns number columns and rounds floating-point noise for display only, so sorting, editing, and export keep the raw value. Missing values show as NULL. See [Attribute Table](https://geolibre.app/user-guide/attribute-table/).
• **Terrain and QGIS projects**：a custom COG DEM can be surrounded, and its no-data gaps filled, by the global terrain instead of a flat plain. QGIS project import now brings in WMS and XYZ layers, remote GeoParquet, and the project's default view. See [Projects](https://geolibre.app/user-guide/projects/#importing-a-qgis-project).
• **Traditional Chinese**：the interface ships in Traditional Chinese for Taiwan, Hong Kong, and Macau, bringing it to 23 translations beyond English. See [Internationalization](https://geolibre.app/i18n/).

## Download

Launch GeoLibre Web at https://web.geolibre.app, or get the desktop and mobile apps from https://geolibre.app/downloads/ (or the assets below).
